To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of representational artefacts by public participants and healthcare professionals can help to mediate the gap between policy aims of public participation and actual practices of public participation.

the use of appropriate representational artefact in public participation in health services design can help to structure discussions between public and professional participants and to enable them to engage meaningfully in the design process.
the choice of representational artefacts is crucial to the success of public participation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to enable public participants to meaningfully contribute to the design of health services.
the design of artefacts to support participation.
the design of artefacts that can help to enable the participation of public participants in service improvement and redesign.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
using representational artefact in public participation in health services is a good idea.
representational artefacts are an effective means of enabling meaningful public participation in service improvement projects.
the use of representational artefacts is a useful way for public participation in health services design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are exploring how to use design as a method for public participation in healthcare.
the use of artefacts can be a way to structure the interaction between the public and health professionals, and to make the interaction meaningful and valid for both groups.

the use of representational artefacts in the context of participatory design in healthcare can help to structure meaningful discussions between public participants, healthcare professionals and designers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of representational artefacts in public participatory processes can enable meaningful participation.
using representational artefact can help to mediate interactions in a way that is meaningful to both the public and the professionals.
using representational artefact can provide an alternative to the current focus in the literature on the professionalisation and skills development of public participants.
